summary:
Welcome to EarthSound! For The Earth Information Jukebox Challenge, we didn’t just build an audio player—we built a barrier-free, multi-sensory symphony of our changing planet powered by real NASA satellite data.

Today, Earth science is overwhelmingly visual, locking out 285 million blind and low-vision people worldwide. Instead of converting pixels into harsh, fatiguing synthesizer noise, EarthSound transforms 11 official NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations, GIBS satellite layers, and live NASA POWER telemetry into a 5-voice acoustic orchestra.

But this isn’t just passive listening—it’s you conducting the planet. From the very first touch or keystroke, our Zero-UI voice guide welcomes you into an eyes-free journey across the globe: hear the Double Bass pulse with global carbon dioxide, the Grand Piano trace the Amazon forest canopy, the Violin follow Gulf Stream thermal currents, and the Saxophone ignite with urban night lights. Step through 16 spatial scan segments, probe any coordinate with Tactile Sonar, edit notes, and export verified DOCX scientific reports alongside lossless WAV and MIDI files. This is NASA data like you’ve never experienced it before—not silent in charts, but alive as a universal planetary language.
details:
1. EXECUTIVE OVERVIEW: WHAT EARTHSOUND DOES & HOW IT WORKS EarthSound ("See the Earth. Hear its data.") is an interactive planetary jukebox and WCAG AAA-compliant scientific sonification studio built for The Earth Information Jukebox challenge. It transforms 11 official NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) and Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) visualizations, live NASA GIBS WMTS satellite imagery, and real-time NASA POWER agroclimatology telemetry into a harmonious 5-stem acoustic orchestra in real time.

EarthSound operates via a 4-Layer Architecture and 8-Step Signal Flow:

Layer 01 — Ingestion (Steps 1–2): Ingests 11 curated NASA EIC/SVS datasets, live NASA GIBS WMTS satellite map tiles (with 0–100% opacity control), global geocoding (countries, cities, oceans, glaciers), and live NASA POWER Agroclimatology API telemetry (T2M surface temperature, PRECTOTCORR precipitation, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN solar irradiance, RH2M humidity, WS10M wind speed) by exact coordinates and date (MM/DD/YYYY).

Layer 02 — Computer Vision DSP (Steps 3–4): Decomposes an $800 \times 400\text{ px}$ satellite frame into 16 spatial segments ($50\text{ px}$ vertical slices: Segment 1 to Segment 16) and a 16-bin RGB spectral histogram. Computes ITU-R BT.709 relative luminance ($L = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B$, note activation threshold $L > 30$), contrast standard deviation ($\sigma$), and spatial edge density (%).

Layer 03 — Caldwell 73 Harmonic Engine (Steps 5–6): Applies the NASA Caldwell 73 mathematical model ($Y$-coordinate latitude $\rightarrow$ pitch; BT.709 luminance $L \rightarrow$ velocity/BPM; RGB dominance $\rightarrow$ instrument voice). Instead of raw oscillator frequencies that produce ear-fatiguing noise, all notes are strictly quantized to consonant modal chord progressions (e.g., F Lydian Cosmic Orchestra: Fmaj7#11 – G6 – Em7 – Am9 at 92 BPM; D Dorian at 118 BPM).

Layer 04 — 5-Stem Acoustic Synthesis & Export (Steps 7–8): Synthesizes 5 simultaneous, polyphony-safe acoustic voices generating 80 editable notes ($16 \times 5$) in an interactive Piano Roll, with instant export to lossless .wav, multi-track .mid (MIDI), and verified .docx scientific reports.

2. SCIENTIFIC SONIFICATION MATRIX (5 ORCHESTRA VOICES × 11 NASA DATASETS) Each of the 5 channels has independent Mute, Solo, Volume, and single-key studio shortcuts (Keys 1–5), allowing researchers to isolate individual Earth systems by ear:

Ch 1 — Acoustic Double Bass (Key 1): Macro background, ocean depth, baseline $\text{CO}_2$ concentration, Red spectrum (Warm Dust & Bass Foundation) $\rightarrow$ DYAMOND Global $\text{CO}_2$ (SVS 5196), GEOS Aerosols (SVS 5572).

Ch 2 — Concert Grand Piano & Strings (Key 2): Structural coordinates, forest canopy elevation, Green spectrum (Mid-Spectrum Harmonic Core) $\rightarrow$ GEDI Forest Height (SVS 4950), Change in Night Lights 2012–2023 (SVS 5313).

Ch 3 — Orchestral Violin (Key 3): Sustained melodic contours, ocean thermal gradients, Blue spectrum (Stellar Filament Harmonics) $\rightarrow$ Global Sea Surface Currents & Temperature (SVS 3912), Perpetual Ocean 2 (SVS 5425), Data Sonification: Caldwell 73 (SVS 13786).

Ch 4 — Alto Saxophone (Key 4): High-energy activity peaks, urban illumination contrast, orbital lightning flashes ($L > 240$) $\rightarrow$ ISS Lightning Events 2017–2023 (SVS 5011), Night Lights (SVS 5313), Air Quality Model Runs (SVS 5533).

Ch 5 — Concert Flute & Chimes (Key 5): Upper-atmosphere streams, 3D moisture density, polar albedo $\rightarrow$ 3D View of an Atmospheric River (SVS 4960), GEOS Sea Salt Aerosols (SVS 5572), EIC Content Database.

3. KEY DIFFERENTIATORS: WHY EARTHSOUND STANDS OUT

Solving the "Blind Entry Paradox" (Zero-UI Voice Onboarding): A blind user never has to visually search for an accessibility button. The very first keystroke or mouse-wheel scroll triggers a soft female voice narrator (0.86x default pace, 0.94 pitch), guiding the user to select Keyboard Mode (double-press Space/Enter) or Mouse-Assisted Mode (scroll wheel / double-click).

Four Stateful UI Modes with Zero State Loss:

01. Standard Mode: Silent visual telemetry studio (voice narrator completely muted for sighted users).

02. High Contrast Mode (WCAG AAA): Pure monochrome surfaces with 2px borders across 100% of tabs and tables.

03. Low Vision Mode: 22px typography, 48px touch targets, and responsive UI/Chart/Table scaling (100%, 125%, 150%).

04. Accessibility First Mode: Full screen-reader (NVDA/VoiceOver) & spoken UI navigation, Smart Audio Ducking (-6 dB) that lowers music volume whenever the narrator speaks, and OS-adaptive hotkeys.

Multi-Sensory Pattern-Coded Colorbar Legend: Eliminates color-only barriers for colorblind and blind users by encoding every luminance bracket (15 to 250) with 5 tactile geometric patterns (DOTS, DIAGONAL, GRID, HORIZONTAL, CROSSHATCH), physical descriptions, reference notes (F2 to F5), and audition triggers.

Interactive 80-Note Piano Roll & Two-Segment Comparison (Key C): Users can edit pitch, duration (4n/8n/2n), segment timing (Seg 1–16), velocity, and instrument for all 80 notes, or scientifically compare two spatial regions (e.g., Segment 3 at 17.4 luminance vs. Segment 12 at 75.0 luminance, $\Delta +57.6$) with back-to-back audio playback.

End-to-End Scientific & Creative Export (.docx + .wav + .mid): Exports a complete Microsoft Word (.docx) agroclimatology and 16-segment telemetry report with an interactive push prompt to download the exact matching live-buffer .wav audio and multi-track .mid files for DAWs.

4. BENEFITS, TARGET AUDIENCE & INTENDED IMPACT

Blind & Low-Vision Researchers (285M+ globally): Independent, eyes-free exploration of global satellite maps, NASA telemetry, and 16-segment data tables without visual assistance.

Earth Scientists & Climatologists: Rapid cross-referencing of visual satellite layers with quantitative NASA POWER parameters and instant .docx report generation.

STEM Educators & Students: Engaging multi-sensory learning via the Learn workspace and Earth Observation News feed (featuring PACE, GEOS, ISS GEDI Lidar, and Perpetual Ocean 2 dispatches with one-click Read Article Aloud).

Musicians & Sound Designers: Transforming planetary climate shifts into editable, studio-grade 5-channel MIDI and WAV compositions.

5. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE STACK

Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Tone.js (Web Audio API polyphonic synthesis, limiters & live recording), HTML5 Canvas 2D API (pixel matrix DSP), Leaflet.js (GIS & NASA GIBS WMTS overlays), Chart.js (scalable 16-bin RGB histograms), Web Speech API & Gemini TTS voice profile, WAI-ARIA / WCAG 2.2 Level AAA architecture.

Backend & Export Engine: Python, FastAPI, OpenCV, Pillow, NumPy, MIDIUtil (binary multi-track .mid serialization), docx document generation engine.

APIs & Data Sources: NASA SVS & EIC Content Database (11 datasets), NASA GIBS WMTS, NASA Langley POWER Agroclimatology REST API, OpenStreetMap Nominatim & Open-Meteo Geocoding API.

6. FACTORS CONSIDERED BY OUR TEAM

Auditory Ergonomics: Replacing harsh raw sine/square oscillators with warm acoustic instrument envelopes and modal harmonic quantization so users can analyze data for hours without ear fatigue.

Audio Collision Prevention: Implementing automated -6 dB audio ducking so screen readers and sonification music never clash.

Scientific Transparency: Clearly distinguishing between physical satellite telemetry (NASA POWER / BT.709 luminance) and musical pitch encoding, with automatic verification badges.

Universal Free Access: Designing a 100% open, zero-paywall, privacy-safe web platform that runs directly in any modern browser without external hardware.
